summary: A top-five global economy and technological powerhouse, pacifist by constitution since 1947 but rearming amid regional threats. The cornerstone of the US alliance system in Asia and a leading donor and investor across the Indo-Pacific.

history.detail: US warships force Japan to open after centuries of isolation.
Rapid modernisation and industrialisation transform Japan into a great power.
Russo-Japanese War; first modern Asian victory over a European power.
Attack on the US brings America into World War II.
Hiroshima and Nagasaki destroyed; Japan surrenders, US occupation begins.
Article 9 renounces war; US drafts the postwar democratic order.
Symbol of Japan's postwar 'economic miracle' recovery.
Start of the 'Lost Decades' of stagnation and deflation.
Earthquake and tsunami trigger a nuclear meltdown; energy policy upended.
Japan pledges to double defence spending to 2% of GDP, its biggest shift since 1945.

finance.currency_role: Japanese yen; a major global reserve and safe-haven currency
finance.central_bank: Bank of Japan (1882); pioneer of zero/negative rates and QE

tech_startups.vc_ecosystem: Growing but conservative; SoftBank's Vision Fund a global force

resources.oil_gas: Almost entirely import-dependent for energy; major LNG buyer
resources.nuclear: Restarting reactors post-Fukushima to cut fossil imports
resources.rare_earths: Reliant on imports; invested in Australian supply to bypass China
resources.agriculture: Low self-sufficiency; heavily protected rice sector
resources.water: Abundant; mountainous terrain limits arable land

follow_the_money.detail: Decades of trade surpluses make Japan the biggest net holder of overseas assets.
Ultra-low rates let investors borrow yen to buy higher-yielding assets worldwide — a global market force.
Major infrastructure financier across Southeast Asia, competing with China's Belt and Road.

theories_disputed.detail: Imperial Japan's biological-warfare unit conducted lethal human experiments; the US granted immunity to researchers for their data after WWII.
Politicians' visits to a shrine honouring war criminals repeatedly inflame China and South Korea; framed as remembrance vs. revisionism.

connections.detail: Security treaty; ~50,000 US troops based in Japan
Senkaku Islands dispute; economic interdependence with tension
Rocky history but thawing security cooperation vs. shared threats
Missile overflights and abduction issue keep tensions high
Quasi-ally; reciprocal access and Quad partner
